title: Wish / if only
note: wish + past simple / past perfect / would · if only · could · did not have to · 4 strands x 12 · 48 items · built to live 2026-08-06 (cloud run 5)

cards.title: The tense goes one step back
cards.body: After **wish**, English moves the verb one tense back from the time you mean. A regret about **now** uses the **past simple**; a regret about the **past** uses the **past perfect**. The past tense here is not past time — it is distance from reality.
cards.body_cz: Po **wish** posune angličtina sloveso o jeden čas zpátky oproti času, který máte na mysli. Lítost nad **teď** používá **minulý prostý**, lítost nad **minulostí** používá **předminulý čas**. Minulý čas tu neznamená minulost — znamená odstup od skutečnosti.

table.caption: Which tense after wish
rows: I wish I had more time.
I wish you had told me earlier.
I wish I could speak German.

cards.title: were for every person
cards.body: With **be**, the form after wish is **were** for I, he, she and it as well. **was** is heard in speech and is accepted here, but **were** is the form to learn.
cards.body_cz: U slovesa **be** je po wish tvar **were** i pro I, he, she a it. **was** se v mluvené řeči slyší a uznáváme ho, ale učte se **were**.
points: If only we were on holiday.

cards.title: wish + would is about somebody else
cards.title_cz: wish + would se týká někoho jiného
cards.body: **would** is for behaviour you want changed — usually somebody else's, and usually with a note of annoyance. You cannot use it about your own situation: not "I wish I would be taller".
cards.body_cz: **would** se používá pro chování, které chcete změnit — obvykle cizí a obvykle s nádechem naštvání. O vlastní situaci ho použít nelze: ne „I wish I would be taller“.
points: I wish my brother would clean his room. (he refuses)
If only it would stop raining. (the weather will not change)
For your own state use the past simple instead: I wish I were taller.

cards.title: if only = wish, with more feeling
cards.title_cz: if only = wish, jen s větším důrazem
cards.body: **if only** follows exactly the same tense rules as **wish** and is simply stronger. It often stands alone as a whole sentence.
cards.body_cz: **if only** se řídí úplně stejnými pravidly časů jako **wish**, jen je důraznější. Často stojí samostatně jako celá věta.
points: If only we had left earlier. (past perfect — regret about the past)
If only I knew the way. (past simple — regret about now)
If only he would help us. (would — somebody else's behaviour)

table.caption: Avoid / Say
rows: I wish I have more time.
I wish I would be taller.
would is not for your own state
I wish you would have told me.
She wishes she must not work.
She wishes she **did not have to** work.

items.en: I wish I had more time.
items.gap: I wish I ____ more time.
accepts: I wish I had more time.
items.explanation: wish + past simple = a regret about how things are NOW. The past tense is not past time.
items.explanation_cz: wish + minulý prostý = lítost nad tím, jak to je TEĎ. Minulý čas tu neznamená minulost.
